stem:
Trimethylamine reacts with bromoethane by {{SN2}}. Reaction A is run in 25:75 water:ethanol and reaction B in 50:50 water:ethanol. Which is faster? Explain using the transition state, and sketch the energy curve for each solvent.
[[rxn:CN(C)C + CCBr>>CC[N+](C)(C)C.[Br-]]]
model:
B is faster. The starting materials are neutral. In the transition state charge is forming: [{{(CH3)3N}}δ+···{{CH2CH3}}···Brδ-]‡. The more polar solvent (more water) solvates these partial charges, so it stabilizes the transition state more than it stabilizes the starting materials. That lowers {{Ea}}.

A, less polar:

[[energy:R=0,TS=24,P=-4]]

B, more polar (the top drops more than the start):

[[energy:R=-1,TS=19,P=-10]]

rubric.h: B, the more polar solvent, is faster
Transition state drawn or described with δ+ on N and δ- on Br
The polar solvent stabilizes the transition state more than the starting materials, so Ea is lower
Two energy curves with the smaller barrier for B

steps.h: Trimethylamine and bromoethane are both neutral molecules.

ask.q: What is the total charge on the starting materials?
ask.a: Zero, and neither molecule carries any full charge.

steps.h: The N-C bond is half made and the C-Br bond is half broken: [N<sup>δ+</sup>···C···Br<sup>δ-</sup>]. Charge is being created.

ask.a: Nitrogen. It is giving its lone pair to carbon.

steps.h: B has more water, so B is the more polar solvent.
Solvent molecules gather around the partial charges of the transition state. The neutral starting materials gain little. So the transition state drops more than the starting materials.

ask.q: Which level moves more, the start or the top?

steps.h: A lower transition state with almost the same starting level means a smaller {{Ea}}. B is faster.

solution.rule: Neutral reactants, charged transition state: more polar solvent, faster.

stem:
Methoxide reacts with the trimethylsulfonium ion by {{SN2}}. Reaction A is run in methanol, reaction B in 50:50 water:methanol. Which is faster, and why?
[[rxn:C[O-] + C[S+](C)C>>COC + CSC]]

choices.h: A, because the more polar solvent stabilizes the charged starting materials more than the transition state
choices.why: This is the lecture's second case. The full charges at the start are solvated better than the partial charges at the top, so more polarity raises {{Ea}}.

choices.h: B, because a more polar solvent always speeds up a reaction between ions
choices.why: Polarity helps only when there is more charge in the transition state than at the start. Here there is less.

choices.h: B, because the transition state has partial charges that the polar solvent stabilizes
choices.why: It does stabilize them, but less than it stabilizes the full charges of the starting materials. The comparison is what matters.

choices.h: The rates are the same, because the products are neutral
choices.why: The rate depends on the starting materials and the transition state, not on the products.

steps.h: A full negative charge on methoxide and a full positive charge on sulfur. Both ions are strongly solvated.

ask.q: Are the starting materials neutral or charged?

steps.h: [{{CH3O}}<sup>δ-</sup>···{{CH3}}···S<sup>δ+</sup>]: each charge has shrunk to a partial charge on the way to two neutral products. Charge is being destroyed.

ask.q: Is there more or less charge in the transition state than at the start?

steps.t: What the more polar solvent does
steps.h: B (with water) stabilizes everything that is charged, but it stabilizes the two full charges of the starting materials more than the two partial charges of the transition state.
The start drops more than the top, so {{Ea}} is larger in B. The less polar solvent, A, is faster.

ask.q: Which level drops more in B?

solution.answer: A (methanol, the less polar solvent) is faster.
solution.rule: Charged reactants, less charge in the transition state: more polar solvent, slower.

stem:
tert-Butyl bromide reacts by {{SN1}} in mixtures of water and ethanol. Is it faster in 20:80 water:ethanol or in 50:50 water:ethanol? Explain, naming the step and the transition state that matter.
[[mol:CC(C)(C)Br]]
model:
Faster in 50:50 water:ethanol. The rate-determining step of {{SN1}} is ionization: [[rxn:CC(C)(C)Br>>C[C+](C)C + [Br-]]]

The starting compound is neutral. The transition state is [{{(CH3)3C}}δ+···Brδ-]‡, with charge developing. The more polar solvent stabilizes this transition state more than the starting compound, which lowers {{Ea}} of the rate-determining step. The protic solvent also hydrogen-bonds to the leaving bromide.

[[energy:R=0,TS1=22,I=12,TS2=15,P=-6|I=carbocation,TS1=rate-determining]]

rubric.h: The more polar solvent (50:50) is faster
Names ionization (loss of bromide) as the rate-determining step
Transition state with δ+ on carbon and δ- on bromine
Polar solvent stabilizes that transition state more than the neutral starting compound, lowering Ea
Mentions that the protic solvent solvates the leaving bromide, or sketches the two-step curve with the first hump higher

steps.t: Find the step that sets the rate
steps.h: {{SN1}}: rate = k[t-BuBr]. The rate-determining step is the first one, ionization of the C-Br bond.

ask.q: Which species are in the transition state of this step?
ask.a: Only the alkyl bromide (with solvent around it). The nucleophile is not involved yet.

steps.h: tert-Butyl bromide is a neutral molecule.
The C-Br bond is stretching: [{{(CH3)3C}}<sup>δ+</sup>···Br<sup>δ-</sup>]. Charge is being created on the way to a carbocation and bromide.
The more polar solvent (50:50, more water) stabilizes this transition state more than the neutral starting compound, so {{Ea}} is lower.
Water and ethanol are protic: they hydrogen-bond to the departing bromide, which helps it leave.

solution.answer: Faster in 50:50 water:ethanol, the more polar solvent.
solution.rule: SN1: more polar solvent, faster ionization.

stem:
1-Bromobutane reacts with NaCN by {{SN2}}. In which solvent is the reaction faster?
[[rxn:CCCCBr + [C-]#N.[Na+]>>CCCCC#N + [Na+].[Br-]]]

choices.h: DMSO, because it cannot hydrogen-bond to cyanide, so the nucleophile is free
choices.why: A polar aprotic solvent does not cage the anion. The lecture summary lists polar aprotic solvents for {{SN2}}.

choices.h: Methanol, because a polar protic solvent stabilizes the charged transition state
choices.why: No charge is created here. The charge is more concentrated on the starting cyanide, and methanol stabilizes that more than the transition state.

choices.h: Methanol, because sodium cyanide dissolves better in it
choices.why: Dissolving the salt is not the issue: DMSO dissolves it too. Methanol's hydrogen bonds hold the anion back.

choices.h: The same in both, because both solvents are polar
choices.why: Polar is not the whole story. Protic or aprotic decides how tightly the anion is held.

steps.h: The nucleophile is an anion with a full negative charge. The substrate is neutral.

ask.q: Where is the charge at the start?

steps.h: [NC<sup>δ-</sup>···C···Br<sup>δ-</sup>]: the same single negative charge, now spread over two atoms. No new charge is created.

ask.q: Is the charge more concentrated at the start or in the transition state?

steps.h: Methanol hydrogen-bonds to cyanide and holds it tightly. That stabilizes the starting nucleophile more than the spread-out transition state, so the barrier is higher. The cyanide has to shed solvent before it can attack.

steps.t: What a polar aprotic solvent does
steps.h: DMSO dissolves the salt but has no O-H to give to the anion. Cyanide is left free and reactive.

ask.q: Which solvent leaves the nucleophile free?

solution.rule: Anionic nucleophile: polar aprotic solvent for a fast SN2.

stem: Which of these solvents is polar aprotic?

choices.h: DMSO [[mol:CS(C)=O]]
choices.why: Polar S=O bond, and every hydrogen is on carbon: it cannot donate a hydrogen bond.

choices.h: Methanol [[mol:CO]]
choices.why: The O-H makes it a hydrogen-bond donor: polar protic.

choices.h: Acetic acid [[mol:CC(=O)O]]
choices.why: It has an O-H: polar protic. The C=O does not make it aprotic.

choices.h: Hexane [[mol:CCCCCC]]
choices.why: It has no O-H, but it is nonpolar, not polar aprotic.

steps.h: Protic means the solvent has an O-H or N-H and can donate a hydrogen bond. Polar aprotic means polar with no such hydrogen.
Methanol has O-H. Acetic acid has O-H. Hexane is not polar. DMSO, {{(CH3)2SO}}, is polar and has only C-H bonds.
DMSO.

solution.rule: Protic = hydrogen-bond donor (O-H, N-H). DMSO, DMF, acetone and acetonitrile are polar aprotic.

stem:
Triethylamine reacts with iodoethane. Reaction A is run in 25:75 water:ethanol and reaction B in 50:50 water:ethanol. Which is faster?
[[rxn:CCN(CC)CC + CCI>>CC[N+](CC)(CC)CC.[I-]]]

choices.h: B, because the more polar solvent stabilizes the transition state more than the starting materials
choices.why: This is the lecture example: the transition state has δ+ on N and δ- on I, and the starting materials are neutral.

choices.h: A, because the more polar solvent stabilizes the starting materials more
choices.why: The starting materials are neutral and gain little from a polar solvent. This reasoning belongs to the charged-reactant case.

choices.h: A, because water hydrogen-bonds to the nucleophile
choices.why: That argument is for anionic nucleophiles. The lecture result for this neutral amine is that the more polar solvent is faster.

choices.h: Same rate, because the solvent is not in the rate law
choices.why: The solvent is not in the rate law, but it changes k by changing {{Ea}}.

steps.h: Two neutral molecules.
δ+ on N and δ- on I: charge is created.
B has more water and is more polar. It stabilizes the transition state more than the neutral starting materials, so {{Ea}} is lower.

solution.rule: Charge created in the transition state: polar solvent speeds it up.

stem: tert-Butyl bromide reacts with water by {{SN1}} to give tert-butyl alcohol. In which solvent mixture is the reaction fastest?

choices.h: 50:50 water:ethanol
choices.why: The most polar of the three mixtures. It lowers the energy of the ionization transition state the most.

choices.h: 20:80 water:ethanol
choices.why: Less water means a less polar solvent and a slower ionization.

choices.h: 5:95 water:ethanol
choices.why: The least polar mixture gives the slowest ionization.

choices.h: All the same, because rate = k[t-BuBr] and the solvent is not in the rate law
choices.why: The rate law has no solvent term, but k itself depends on the solvent through {{Ea}}.

steps.h: Ionization of the C-Br bond.
Neutral starting compound, transition state with δ+ on C and δ- on Br.
The mixture with the most water is the most polar and stabilizes that transition state best.

solution.rule: Increase the polarity of the solvent, increase the rate of SN1.

stem:
Sodium azide reacts with bromoethane much more slowly in ethanol than in DMF. What is the main reason?
[[rxn:CCBr + [N-]=[N+]=[N-].[Na+]>>CCN=[N+]=[N-] + [Na+].[Br-]]]

choices.h: Ethanol hydrogen-bonds to the azide ion, which stabilizes the nucleophile and raises the barrier
choices.why: A solvated anion is a stabilized starting material. The transition state, with its charge spread out, is stabilized less.

choices.h: Ethanol is too nonpolar to dissolve sodium azide
choices.why: Ethanol is a polar solvent. The problem is the hydrogen bonds it makes to the anion.

choices.h: DMF hydrogen-bonds to the bromide and pulls it off
choices.why: DMF has no O-H or N-H and cannot donate a hydrogen bond.

choices.h: In DMF the reaction changes to {{SN1}}
choices.why: A primary substrate does not ionize. It is {{SN2}} in both solvents, only faster in DMF.

steps.h: Ethanol is polar protic. DMF is polar aprotic.
Azide is an anion. A protic solvent hydrogen-bonds to it.
The solvated azide is lower in energy and has to lose solvent to attack, so {{Ea}} is larger in ethanol.

solution.answer: Ethanol hydrogen-bonds to the azide ion and stabilizes it.
solution.rule: Protic solvents hold anionic nucleophiles back.

stem: Hydroxide reacts with the trimethylsulfonium ion. The reaction is slower in the more polar solvent. Which explanation is correct? [[rxn:[OH-] + C[S+](C)C>>CO + CSC]]

choices.h: The more polar solvent stabilizes the starting materials more than it stabilizes the transition state
choices.why: The lecture's words: it stabilizes the transition state too, but to a lesser degree, so the barrier is higher.

choices.h: The more polar solvent destabilizes the transition state
choices.why: It does not raise the transition state. It lowers it, only by less than it lowers the starting materials.

choices.h: The more polar solvent stabilizes the neutral products less
choices.why: The products do not affect the rate. Only the starting materials and the transition state do.

choices.h: The more polar solvent reacts with hydroxide and uses it up
choices.why: Nothing is consumed. The effect is on the energies of the levels.

steps.h: Two ions, each with a full charge and a full shell of solvent.
[HO<sup>δ-</sup>···{{CH3}}···S<sup>δ+</sup>]: the charges are being destroyed.
A more polar solvent stabilizes both levels, but the fully charged starting materials more. The gap between them, {{Ea}}, grows.

solution.answer: The more polar solvent stabilizes the charged starting materials more than the transition state.
solution.rule: Charge destroyed in the transition state: polar solvent slows it down.

stem: In a less polar solvent, the reaction of triethylamine with iodoethane has this energy curve: [[energy:R=0,TS=24,P=-4]] Which curve fits the same reaction in a more polar solvent, on the same energy scale?

choices.why: The neutral start barely moves, the partly charged transition state drops, and the ionic product drops most. The barrier falls from 24 to 19.
Here the starting materials drop the most. That is the pattern for charged starting materials, not neutral ones.
Only the product is lowered. The transition state already carries partial charges, so it must drop as well.

choices.h: [[energy:R=0,TS=30,P=-4]]
choices.why: A polar solvent does not raise the energy of a transition state that has charge on it.

steps.h: Neutral starting materials: almost no change. Transition state with δ+ and δ-: lowered clearly. Ionic product: lowered the most.
Start close to 0, top well below 24, product well below -4.
From -1 to 18 is 19, smaller than 24: faster, as the lecture says.

solution.answer: The curve that starts at about the same level, with a lower top and a lower product.
solution.rule: The solvent lowers each level in proportion to its charge.

stem:
tert-Butyl chloride ionizes readily in water but hardly at all in hexane. Explain why the {{SN1}} reaction needs a polar protic solvent. Describe the transition state of the slow step in your answer.
[[mol:CC(C)(C)Cl]]
model: The rate-determining step is ionization of the C-Cl bond. The starting compound is neutral, and the transition state is [{{(CH3)3C}}δ+···Clδ-]‡. Water is polar, so it stabilizes this transition state (and the ions after it) more than it stabilizes the neutral starting compound, which lowers {{Ea}}. Water is also protic: its O-H groups hydrogen-bond to the chloride as it leaves. Hexane is nonpolar and can do neither, so the barrier to making ions is too high.

rubric.h: Slow step is ionization to a carbocation and chloride
Transition state has δ+ on carbon and δ- on chlorine
Polar solvent stabilizes the transition state more than the neutral starting compound, so Ea is lower
Protic solvent hydrogen-bonds to (solvates) the leaving anion

steps.h: Ionization: the C-Cl bond breaks to give a carbocation and chloride.
[{{(CH3)3C}}<sup>δ+</sup>···Cl<sup>δ-</sup>]: charge is forming from a neutral molecule.
Water molecules surround the partial charges and lower the energy of the transition state more than that of the neutral chloride. Hexane cannot do this, so the barrier stays very high.
Water donates hydrogen bonds to the departing chloride, which stabilizes the leaving group as it forms.

solution.answer: A polar protic solvent stabilizes the charge-separated transition state of ionization, and hydrogen-bonds to the leaving anion.
solution.rule: SN1 is favoured by polar protic solvents.

stem: Each reaction is moved to a more polar solvent. Which one becomes slower?

choices.h: [[rxn:[OH-] + C[S+](C)C>>CO + CSC]]
choices.why: Both reactants are ions. Their charge is disappearing in the transition state, so a more polar solvent favours the starting materials and raises the barrier.

choices.h: [[rxn:CCN(CC)CC + CCI>>CC[N+](CC)(CC)CC.[I-]]]
choices.why: Neutral reactants and a transition state with δ+ and δ-: faster in the more polar solvent.

choices.h: [[rxn:CC(C)(C)Br>H2O;>CC(C)(C)O]]
choices.why: {{SN1}}: the neutral substrate ionizes, so more polarity means a faster reaction.

choices.h: [[rxn:c1ccncc1 + CI>>C[n+]1ccccc1.[I-]]]
choices.why: The same type as the triethylamine reaction: two neutral molecules making charge.

steps.t: Sort by the charge on the starting materials
steps.h: Three of the four start from neutral molecules and build charge in the transition state. One starts from two ions.
Neutral start, charge created: faster in a more polar solvent. Charged start, charge destroyed: slower.

steps.t: Pick the one with ions at the start
steps.h: Hydroxide and trimethylsulfonium.

solution.rule: Look at where the charge is at the start and at the top.

stem:
A student predicts that {{HS-}} and {{CH3I}} react faster in methanol than in DMSO, "because the transition state is charged and methanol stabilizes charge". The reaction is in fact much faster in DMSO. What is wrong with the prediction?
[[rxn:[SH-] + CI>>CS + [I-]]]

choices.h: The charge is not created in the transition state. It is already on {{HS-}}, where methanol's hydrogen bonds stabilize it more than in the transition state
choices.why: The comparison that matters is start against top. The concentrated charge of the free anion is solvated better than the spread-out charge of the transition state.

choices.h: Methanol is less polar than hexane
choices.why: Methanol is a polar solvent. Polarity is not where the prediction fails.

choices.h: The transition state of an {{SN2}} reaction has no charge at all
choices.why: It carries the full negative charge of the nucleophile, shared between S and I.

choices.h: In methanol the reaction becomes {{SN1}}, which is slower
choices.why: A methyl cation never forms. The mechanism is {{SN2}} in both solvents.

steps.t: Count the charge at the start
steps.h: One full negative charge, all on sulfur.

steps.t: Count it in the transition state
steps.h: [HS<sup>δ-</sup>···{{CH3}}···I<sup>δ-</sup>]: still one negative charge in total, now spread over S and I. No charge was created.

Methanol hydrogen-bonds strongly to the concentrated charge on {{HS-}} and less well to the spread-out charge of the transition state. The start drops more than the top, so {{Ea}} is larger in methanol.
It cannot hydrogen-bond to the anion, so {{HS-}} is not held back.

solution.answer: The transition state has no more charge than the starting nucleophile, and methanol stabilizes the starting anion more.
solution.rule: Compare the transition state with the starting materials, not with zero.

stem:
Hydroxide reacts with the triethylsulfonium ion by {{SN2}}. Is the reaction faster in ethanol or in 50:50 water:ethanol? Explain using the charges on the starting materials and on the transition state, and sketch the energy curve for each solvent.
[[rxn:[OH-] + CC[S+](CC)CC>>CCO + CCSCC]]
model:
Faster in ethanol. Both starting materials are ions and are well solvated. In the transition state [HOδ-···{{CH2CH3}}···Sδ+{{(CH2CH3)2}}]‡ the charges are being destroyed. The more polar solvent stabilizes the starting materials more (greater solvation). It stabilizes the transition state too, but to a lesser degree, so {{Ea}} is larger.

Ethanol, less polar:

[[energy:R=0,TS=20,P=-15]]

50:50 water:ethanol, more polar (the start drops more than the top):

[[energy:R=-8,TS=17,P=-16]]

rubric.h: Ethanol, the less polar solvent, is faster
Both starting materials carry full charges and are solvated
Transition state with δ- on O and δ+ on S: charge is being destroyed
More polar solvent stabilizes the starting materials more than the transition state, so Ea is larger
Two energy curves with the larger barrier in the more polar solvent

steps.h: Hydroxide (full minus) and the sulfonium ion (full plus). Both are strongly solvated.
[HO<sup>δ-</sup>···{{CH2CH3}}···S<sup>δ+</sup>]: the O-C bond is forming and the C-S bond is breaking, and both charges are fading towards the neutral products.
50:50 water:ethanol stabilizes both levels, but the full charges at the start more than the partial charges at the top.
The start drops more than the top, so {{Ea}} is larger in the more polar solvent. Ethanol alone is faster.

solution.answer: Faster in ethanol, the less polar solvent.
solution.rule: Charged reactants, charge destroyed: less polar solvent is faster.

stem:
The same {{SN2}} reaction was followed in two solvents, drawn on one energy scale. Which statement fits both curves?
Solvent X: [[energy:R=0,TS=20,P=-12]]
Solvent Y: [[energy:R=-7,TS=18,P=-13]]

choices.h: Y is the more polar solvent, the starting materials are charged, and the reaction is slower in Y
choices.why: The start falls by 7 and the top by 2, so the barrier grows from 20 to 25: the charged-reactant case.

choices.h: Y is the more polar solvent, the starting materials are neutral, and the reaction is faster in Y
choices.why: Neutral starting materials would hardly move. Here the start moves the most, and the barrier is larger in Y.

choices.h: The reaction is faster in Y because its transition state is lower
choices.why: The rate depends on the gap from start to top, not on the height of the top alone. The gap is 25 in Y and 20 in X.

choices.h: X is the more polar solvent, because the reaction is faster in it
choices.why: Faster does not mean more polar. Y lowers every charged level, which marks it as the more polar solvent.

steps.h: X: 20 - 0 = 20. Y: 18 - (-7) = 25. The reaction is slower in Y.
From X to Y the start dropped by 7 and the top by only 2. Y stabilizes the starting materials much more than the transition state.
A solvent that stabilizes the start strongly is the more polar one, and the starting materials must be charged, with less charge in the transition state.

solution.answer: Y is the more polar solvent and the starting materials are ions.
solution.rule: The level that drops most is the one with the most charge.

stem: 1-Bromopropane and NaCN react by {{SN2}} in dry DMSO. To make the solvent "more polar" a student adds a large amount of water. What happens to the rate?

choices.h: It decreases, because water hydrogen-bonds to cyanide and stabilizes the nucleophile
choices.why: The free anion in DMSO becomes a caged, lower-energy anion in water, and the barrier grows.

choices.h: It increases, because a more polar solvent stabilizes the transition state
choices.why: The transition state has no more charge than the starting cyanide, so extra polarity gives no advantage, and the hydrogen bonds cost rate.

choices.h: It does not change, because water is not in the rate law
choices.why: Rate = k[RBr][{{CN-}}], but k depends on the solvent.

choices.h: It increases, because water turns the reaction into {{SN1}}
choices.why: A primary carbocation does not form, so there is no {{SN1}} pathway to switch to.

steps.h: The charge is on the starting cyanide and is only spread out in the transition state. More polarity does not help this type of reaction.
Water is protic. It hydrogen-bonds to cyanide.
The solvated cyanide is stabilized more than the transition state, so {{Ea}} rises and the reaction slows.

solution.rule: For an anionic nucleophile, protic solvent slows SN2 even though it is polar.
